name: Learn basic watercolour painting
blurb: Watercolour is a water-control skill. Learn the four core techniques and how long each wash takes to dry, and the medium stops fighting you.
gear: A small pan set of artist-grade paint (student paint is a false economy)
A round brush, size 8 or 10, and two water jars
steps: Use proper paper. Thin paper buckles and ruins everything, and no amount of skill compensates.
Learn the four techniques: flat wash, graded wash, wet-on-wet and dry brush, practising each on a whole page.
Learn water ratios by making a value scale of one colour from nearly black to nearly nothing.
Learn to preserve the white of the paper by planning your highlights — watercolour has no white paint worth using.
Learn to leave it alone. Working back into a drying wash creates the blooms and mud that define beginner work.
Paint the same simple subject — a pear, a sky — ten times, working from light to dark.
tips: Mud comes from overworking and from mixing too many pigments. Two-colour mixes stay clean.
Watercolour dries lighter than it looks wet. Mix stronger than you think you need.
Stretch or tape the paper down before starting.
proof: A painting with clean washes, preserved whites, and no muddy or blotchy areas.
